To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HER-2/NEU oncogene is expressed in follicular adenomas of the thyroid gland and the c-MYC oncogene is expressed less often in benign follicular adenomas than in malignant follicular neoplastic lesions.
the HER-2 oncogene is not expressed in follicular neoplasm of the thyroid.

the incidence of c-myc oncogenic expression in malignant follicular neoplastic thyroid lesions is significantly greater than that of benign follicular lesions, but that c-myc expression does not appear useful as a prognostic indicator for patients with follicular carcinoma.

the study of oncogenes in thyroid follicular neoplastic lesions.
the role of oncogenes in follicular thyroid tumors.
the role of the HER- 2/neu and the c-myc oncogenesis in the thyroid gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oncogene expression is not a reliable marker of aggressiveness in follicular thyroid tumors.
c-myc oncogenic expression is a poor marker in follicular thyroid carcinoma, and its expression does not correlate with prognosis.
c-myc oncogenic expression is not useful in the diagnosis of follicular thyroid cancer.

oncogene expression is more frequent in malignant follicular neoplastic lesions, but is not a good predictor of biologic behavior.
the expression of HER-2/neuc-myc is a potential marker for malignant transformation in follicular thyroid neoplasms, but it does not appear to have prognostic significance.
c-myc expression is not a good marker for prognosis in follicular thyroid carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HER-2/ neu oncogene is not a marker for follicular neoplastic disease of the thyroid.
c-myc expression is not associated with the development of metastasis in follicular thyroid carcinomas.
